subject: CDBG Annual Action Plan and Equity Theft Support
overview: The Council approved the $1.25 million Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Annual Action Plan and passed a resolution supporting state legislation to ban 'equity theft' in tax foreclosures. The body also addressed an Open Meeting Law complaint, approved a Tufts University lodging house license, and referred a veteran housing incentive program to committee.

items.title: Ceremonial recognitions and orchestra performance
items.summary: The Council honored the gold medal-winning Medford High School String Orchestra, the silver medal-winning middle school ensemble, and students from Brooks Elementary for their fundraiser supporting postal worker safety.

items.title: Approval of records and committee reports
items.summary: The Council approved meeting records from April 30 and committee reports from the Budget, Community Development Block Grant, Resident Services, and Planning and Permitting committees.

items.title: Veteran housing incentives referral
items.summary: A resolution to allow the Veteran Services Director to offer financial incentives to landlords renting to qualified veterans was referred to the Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee.

items.title: Open Meeting Law complaint response
items.summary: The Council voted that a social media summary of a previous meeting did not constitute an Open Meeting Law violation and authorized a formal legal response to the Attorney General.

items.title: Executive session for litigation strategy
items.summary: The Council entered into executive session to discuss strategy regarding three specific litigation cases involving the city.

items.title: Finest Auto Body license petition
items.summary: The petition for a Class 2 auto body license and used car sales was tabled until June 11 to allow for zoning research and potential special permit requirements.

items.title: CDBG Program Year 50 Annual Action Plan
items.summary: Following a public hearing, the Council authorized the mayor to submit the $1,252,811 Community Development Block Grant annual action plan to federal authorities.

items.title: Pinky’s Famous Pizza extended hours permit
items.summary: The Council approved an amended request for extended hours until midnight on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, with a requirement for code enforcement reviews at 30 and 60 days.

items.title: Tufts University lodging house license
items.summary: The Council approved a lodging house license for 28 Winthrop Street to accommodate 28 undergraduate students.

items.title: Annual surveillance report
items.summary: The 2023 annual public report required by the city's surveillance ordinance was received and placed on file, noting that no new technologies were approved during the reporting period.

items.title: Support for state legislation to ban equity theft
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution supporting state legislation that would prevent municipalities from seizing the full value of a home to recover smaller tax debts.

items.title: City Council newsletter authorization
items.summary: The Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee was authorized to draft and publish a regular newsletter summarizing Council activities without needing further full-body approval for each issue.
